content.comment_body: Hello, I'm [user_name] from Vietnam. I'm using a USB-COM cable and a [product_name] PC cable [article_no], connecting to [product_name] with [article_no]. The software and communication through COM3 seem fine. I can successfully upload small programs from [product_name] to my PC. After modifying the program, I attempt to download it back to [product_name] (compatible with the [version_no]), but the transfer consistently stops at around 50-51% with a "[product_name] response time-out error". This problem occurs even when trying to download previous or empty programs. Can [company_name] support assist with resolving this? Thank you.

Hi, There are two things to check: 1. Which version of [product_name] Soft Comfort are you using? For Windows 7, you need at least version [version_no]. The latest is [product_name] Soft Comfort [version_no]. 2. USB-to-RS232 converters often cause issues; try using a PC with a direct RS232 port or use the official [product_name] USB programming cable ([article_no]). I hope this helps.

This configuration has worked well for controllers like [version_no] and [product_name]... I am able to upload programs without issue. 2. analysis.insight_summary: The user is encountering a persistent '[product_name] response time-out error' at about 50-51% during program downloads from PC to [product_name] hardware. Uploading programs from the device to PC works, but all download attempts, regardless of program size or even empty programs, result in the same issue. Other forum members have identified possible causes such as problems with the USB-to-RS232 converter, running Windows XP through VMware virtualization on Windows 7, and possibly outdated or incompatible [product_name] Soft Comfort software versions. The discussion highlights common hardware interface difficulties and compatibility challenges between [company_name] products, software versions, and modern operating systems.
analysis.user_expectations: The user seeks smooth and reliable program transfers (upload and download) between PC and [product_name] hardware, independent of cable type or OS virtualization. They expect [company_name] hardware and software to function without timeout and compatibility errors.
